items.title: Dan Morgenstern — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s two Italians, Inbimbio and Branfiglio. They were like a comedy team. One was short and the other one was tall. They had a great sense of humor. They said that my eyes were – they said that I had piercing eyes, and they reminded them of Count Dracula, so they called me Drac.

ctx.x: Mannheim. Then we were sent to – from there we were sent to – we were assigned to the Seventh Army – nice patches – and were sent to what was known as the Munich Military Post Service Center, but it was actually Dachau. It was right outside of the small town of

Dachau, not far from where the concentration camp had been. Where we were quartered, in very solid buildings, had been the SS barracks. So that was a nice note. I went once to see Dachau, which had been turned into kind of a museum, but I never spent any time in that small town. I had no eyes for that. But Munich was nearby. It was only – we were about a half hour’s bus ride from Munich. Every time we had a pass or anything like that, we would go into Munich, which was a nice city. Even though Munich was the…
